doc.title: Jack Palmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 24, 1997

title: Harry James, Sinatra's rivalry question and the move to Tommy Dorsey
summary: Palmer retells Sinatra's hiring, says James was a gentleman boss, and that Sinatra left for Dorsey for more money.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: So was there any rivalry between Harry James and Frank Sinatra as far as who was the star here?

Oh, no. Because, no. We were in the Paramount Theatre like I said, and Harry says, “Jack do you want to come with me tonight, I’m going to New Jersey. Remember I told you about that kid singer?” And I said, “I can’t go, I’ve got people from Rome.” But he went that night with Louise, his wife. And the next morning Frank was at the theatre. And then he joined us in New Haven Connecticut like I say. And he didn’t have any tunes and Harry introduced him, and he went out and he sang “Stardust.”
So Frank was always, he knew that Harry was the boss.
He knew that Harry was the boss, is that right? That Harry James was the boss?
Oh, Harry was the leader. That was his boss, yes.
Was he a good guy to work for?
Yeah, great. Yeah he was a gentleman.
And eventually Frank went with Tommy Dorsey?

Yeah. Yeah Harry was a little disturbed about it. But Tommy offered him more money, that was the point. The point was money. And then Tommy was already an established band. And Frank felt that where Harry’s band was a new band, a baby band we used to call it. So Frank thought that was a big move for him, great, which it was at the time, to go with Tommy Dorsey, a big name, already established. Jo Stafford, and the Pied Pipers, was that it?
